$CDNL is down 40% after earnings (and 60% since June), but 7 insiders have stepped in to buy $8.54m of the stock.

Cardinal is a civil contractor providing site-development and infrastructure services - including utilities, grading, paving, and related work - primarily in the southeastern United States.

$35.65/share, $728m mkt cap, $965m EV. 5.9x NTM EV/EBITDA. FY1→FY2 EBITDA growth is 28.0%, and NTM EBITDA margin is 17.1%. FY26 Q2 (ended June 30, 2026) rev grew 114% and EBITDA grew 39.5%, but EBITDA margin was way lower than expected at 12.1%. Only 9 months of historic valuation data v the 36 months required, so no historical medians.

Seven insiders bought $8.54m of the stock. Wood Benjamin (Chief Operating Officer) $1.01m; Zelman Ivy (Director) $500.9k; Spivey Jeremy Simmons (Chief Executive Officer) $3.20m; Wood Anthony Leon Jr. (Director) $2.02m; Rowe Michael Bruce Jr. (Chief Financial Officer) $255.7k; Lee Richard Melvin Jr. (Director) $1.25m; Wimmer Richard Bennett (Director) $293.5k.

Stock fell 36% after earnings and is now down 40% since before earnings. Stock fell because margins came in way lower than expected. Mgmt believes the margin compression is temporary due to the focus on growth - rev guidance increased by over 30% - which required more subcontracted work and coincided with project delays. They are rolling up contractors and service companies to vertically integrate, which mgmt expects will improve margins.

Six Byrna $BYRN insiders buying the post-earnings dip.

They sell less-lethal personal-security launchers, projectiles, aerosols, and accessories through direct-to-consumer, dealer, retail, and professional-security channels.

$3.62/share, $82.1m mkt cap, $73.8m EV. 0.84x NTM EV/rev v 3.23x 3y median (current multiple is 7th percentile and 74.1% below median). FY1→FY2 rev growth is 6.7% (v 20.4% 3y median), NTM EBITDA margin is -4.0% (v 11.2% 3y median). FY26 Q2 (ended May 31, 2026) rev fell 42.5% and EBITDA swung to -$12.1mm.

Six insiders bought $351.3k of the stock across seven trades. Elmore Leonard J (Director) $46.4k; Hughes Herbert (Director) $89.5k; Reed Chris Lavern (Director) $29.6k; Kennedy TJ (Director) $102.3k; Davis Conn Q. (Chief Executive Officer) $76.7k; Kearnes Laurilee (Chief Financial Officer) $6.8k.

Stock fell 34% after earnings and is now down 39% since before earnings. Q2 rev of $16.4m missed consensus by 26% and fell 42.5% YoY: website traffic fell 13%, conversion dropped to 0.59% from 1.0%, average order value fell 19% to ~$302, and dealer reorders slowed as retailers worked through heavy Q1 restocking. 

$9.4m of inventory, equipment-impairment, and product-rationalization charges - partly offset by a $1.1m tariff refund - drove reported gross margin to 11%; total noncash impairments and write-downs were $10.4m and the company posted a $10.1m net loss, although adjusted gross margin was ~62% and adjusted EBITDA was -$0.6mm. 

Mgmt split sales and marketing to create clearer channel accountability; hired HLK to reposition the brand beyond its core audience; is shifting media and influencer spend toward measurable affiliates, Fox Sports, and renewed TV; and is adding personalized product selection to https://t.co/f9cWeXldTH. 

Early tests are encouraging but small: quiz users convert at ~2x the site average, try-before-you-buy converts near 30% and is being expanded 8x, and one retailer's end-cap rollout increased monthly purchases from ~$81k to ~$200k. The pending HERO acquisition is meant to fill the large price gap between Byrna's ~$20 sprays and ~$400 launchers with a ~$250 product; mgmt expects to put HERO on https://t.co/f9cWeXldTH in late Q3/Q4 and create a unified brand experience in FY27 Q1. Mgmt also cut launcher assembly from four lines to two and is producing below the current sales rate, shifted ammunition to lower-cost third parties, and introduced monthly demand-linked production planning; it is targeting a $5m inventory reduction in Q4 and gross margin of at least ~62% for the rest of FY26. 

Early-Q3 traffic and conversion were still roughly unchanged, almost none of the new HLK messaging was live, and marketing expense will increase by ~$250k per month before the revenue arrives; Q3 remains a transition quarter and mgmt expects the more meaningful sales improvement in Q4.

$ONON - trading at lowest-ever EV-EBITDA (9x v 23x median). FY1→FY2 EBITDA growth is 21.1% with 20% margins. Softness in wholesale (mgmt protecting inventory/pricing), but DTC still grew 34%. Big product launches coming in October and April. Co-CEOs each bought $2m https://t.co/oh9EZHlxLK

$DKS - 8.6x EV/EBITDA. Down 30% in the last month because Foot Locker comps fell 3.6%. Core DICK'S store comps were +4.9%. Mgmt protecting share and clearing inventory with promotions.
